issue_context.title: `started` flag for fastify no longer set in v3 on ready()
issue_context.body:
## 🐛 Bug Report

In v3 running `fastify.ready()` no longer sets `fastify[kState].started` to `true`. This results in `lightMyRequest` Chain returned for a builder to be wrapped into a Promise and prematurely resolved, failing with an error.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2257/files

## Expected behavior

Same code would work in v2. Since this is not listed as a breaking change in migration guide, I assume this is a regression rather than removal of deprecated feature.

## Your Environment

- *node version*: 12
- *fastify version*: 3.0.0-rc1
comments: @mcollina I would be happy to work on a fix if you could point me in the right direction. I don't see anything firing a `start` event inside `fastify` itself, so I assume this is a regression inside `avvio`.
@Eomm Any ideas how err case should be handled? Simply throwing it doesn't seem to be a correct solution, it breaks three tests.
You should be ok in doing `res.emit('error', err)`.

> This fails with Error: ERR_AVVIO_READY_TIMEOUT: plugin did not start in time. Am I missing some step that should signal init being completed successfully?

What fails with this?
@mcollina Looks like I was doing something wrong with callback-style ready() initialization. Switched to promise style and it works now. Will cleanup PR now.

review_comments:
Could you add another test without the `.ready().then()`?

You can also switch this to async/await, as this is a v3 specific bug.

Added test with plugin that explicitly returns error; otherwise we'd have to wait until plugin initialization times out, which takes some time, resulting in slower tests. Do you see any disadvantages to that approach?
No, you had a better idea 👍
